The week opens with a mix of regulatory wins, banking
contradictions, and security warnings. Trump's stablecoin company
just secured a federal bank charter. JPMorgan closed Polymarket's
account then tried to land its IPO. Two more hardware wallet
providers disclosed data breaches over the weekend.

Let's dive in.

Latest News
-----------

Trump's Stablecoin Company Just Got a Federal Bank Charter

The OCC granted conditional approval on August 14 for World
Liberty Trust Company, the entity behind the USD1 stablecoin, to
operate as a national trust bank. The approval would allow the
company to take over stablecoin issuance and custody from BitGo,
with a $20 million minimum capital requirement.

USD1 currently carries a $4 billion market cap, ranking fourth
among stablecoins.

What conflict-of-interest concerns did the OCC dismiss during

Some venture further into science-fiction territory, providing scores for IQ and height, or even eye and hair colour. Critics level that fertility entrepreneurs could be this century’s eugenicists. Our leader argues there is an important difference. The world’s biggest fast-food chain is not McDonald’s; it’s not even American. Until now it has made money from bubble tea and ice cream. Soon its servers will be pulling pints, too. Bo Franklin, Senior digital editor What to expect in the week ahead: ▸Japan has just published GDP data. The country’s economy grew by 1.1% on an annualised basis in the second quarter—considerably below analysts’ expectations of 2%. High energy prices caused by the Iran war, weak consumer spending and low investment all contributed to the disappointing figures, though the slow growth was partially offset by strong export figures. ▸ Investors will get a snapshot of how American consumers are feeling this week, as Walmart, Target and Home Depot report earnings. When consumers are stressed about the economy, spending on household goods and clothes are among the first things they shelve. America’s war with Iran has pushed up prices, especially of petrol, hurting the wallets of even prosperous consumers. ▸ On Tuesday Floridians will vote in the state’s primary gubernatorial elections. Voters will decide which Democrat and Republican will battle to become governor in November. Byron Donalds, a Republican congressman, is expected to win his party’s nomination handily, and polls predict he’ll become governor. Florida was once a quintessential swing state—but it has become a bastion of Republican power.
